title: Sign flip under negation
statement:
Let $\sigma\colon\mathrm{Bool}\to\{-1,1\}$ be the sign encoding, so that $\sigma(\mathrm{false})=1$ and $\sigma(\mathrm{true})=-1$. Then for every Boolean value $b$, negating $b$ flips the sign of its encoding:
\[
  \sigma(\lnot b) \;=\; -\,\sigma(b).
\]
hypotheses_covered: b is an arbitrary Boolean value
replaced:
Under the sign encoding $\sigma\colon\mathrm{Bool}\to\{-1,1\}$, the Boolean value
$\mathrm{false}$ is sent to $1$; that is, $\sigma(\mathrm{false}) = 1$.
